comparator.name: Psychology (Dutch)
comparator.sourceNotes: The Dutch Psychology track totals sixty EC per year. Work and Organizational Psychology is selected as the first-listed major on the current Dutch programme page; its major courses are taught in English. Three named six-credit major courses precede the six-credit applied course in year three. The thirty-credit open space includes at least twelve credits from other psychology majors or predefined psychology electives. GROW is zero credit.

components.name: Introduction to Psychology and History of Psychology
Academic Skills Psychology B
components.note: Academic Skills B requires passing Academic Skills A. The first-year sequence completes A before B.

components.name: Academic Skills Psychology C
components.note: Academic Skills C includes information-literacy and plagiarism tests and 20 experimental-subject participation hours. These are part of the first year that must be completed before thesis entry. GROW guidance carries no credit.

components.name: Work Psychology
components.note: This example uses the Work and Organizational Psychology major. Work Psychology, Organizational Psychology and Diversity and Inclusion at Work each carry 6 EC and are taught in English, even within the Dutch track.

components.name: Applied Work and Organizational Psychology
components.note: Applied Work and Organizational Psychology is the 6 EC third-year major course. It applies the PATHS model to an organisational problem with stakeholder feedback, a group presentation, individual logs and required participation.

components.name: Mobility Window: exchange, Psychology minor and electives
components.note: The 30 EC choice space can contain a minor or electives, including study abroad. At least 12 EC must come from non-selected psychology majors or predefined psychology electives. An alternative to this rule requires prior Examination Board approval. No particular choice is assumed.

components.name: Bachelor’s Thesis: Work and Organizational Psychology
components.note: Thesis entry requires all first-year courses and at least 60 EC from later years. The February group is advised to have 138 EC. A quantitative thesis is illustrated; qualitative or systematic-review versions require their corresponding 3 EC elective before submission.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad psychology option is the strongest general response and now includes a stronger organisational strand. Clinical/health development and cognitive/data inquiry remain separately evidenced psychological priorities. Each pair passes the thirty-credit floor. Additional forensic, economic and more narrowly occupational curricula remain coherent possibilities beyond the three-option maximum; the comparator’s illustrative major does not redefine the generic target.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both develop research design, measurement, sampling and evaluation of empirical evidence. UCR also includes statistics and a research project.

Both examine individual differences, motivation and collaboration as influences on effective functioning at work. UCR uses leadership theory and reflective development; Tilburg also covers personnel selection, training and job design.

Both examine inclusion, social differences, belonging and psychological safety in organisational settings. UCR focuses on leadership and emotional processes under pressure and uses an original survey project.
Both examine psychological processes in organisations, including attitudes, motivation, teams, leadership and change, and connect research evidence with organisational problems.
Both examine ethical reasoning and competing responsibilities. Tilburg applies these to professional psychological practice; UCR develops broader moral theory.
Both examine consciousness, mind and accounts of mental states through philosophical argument.
Both introduce sociological theories, institutions, social relationships and inequality.
Both examine biological and neural mechanisms underlying psychological processes.
Both examine perception and action as psychological functions. UCR emphasises neural mechanisms and neuropsychological explanations.
Both relate brain structure, neural processes and psychological functions to behaviour.
Both study social influence, group processes, attitudes and interpersonal behaviour through psychological research.
Both develop regression modelling, statistical assumptions and interpretation of behavioural evidence. UCR also addresses experimental design and other methods.
Both examine classification, explanations and treatment of mental disorders.

Both address psychological testing, reliability, validity and interpretation. Tilburg develops psychometric item analysis and test models; UCR approaches measurement through broader introductory clinical assessment and psychotherapy.
Both examine physical, cognitive, emotional and social development across life stages and theoretical explanations of change.
